TABLE AND INTER-CONVERSION CHARTS FOR ETHANOL-WATER MIXTURES
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adqpted by the Indian Standards Institution on 16 May 1970, after the draft firralized by the Alcohols and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical fivision Council. 0.2 Computation of strength of aqueous solutions containing ethanol at 15.6% is often made in the country from specific gravitv values in air at ,15*6"C and strength is expressed in terms of proof s$rit (proof strength) both in the UK and US Revenue systems. The corresponding percentages of ethanol by weight, and by volume at 15*6"C are ~also `obtained for the various specific gravity values in air at lS$"C. 0.3 The standards IS : 2302-1962* and IS : 3506-1967t are intended for use in obtaining the volumetric content of ethanol at t"C in an ethanolwater mixture from the specific gravity values in vacuum at 15�C by the centesimal hydrometers and by the pyknometer method respectively. 0.4 Various countries have adopted different systems, like proof spirit and ceritesimal hydrometers method to express the percentage of ethanol in an ethanol-water mixture. Subsequent to the publication of IS: 23021962* the need to have a comprehensive table for inter-conversion of various units used in these systems was felt. It is hoped that this standard which incorporates such table and also inter-conversion charts would serve as a ready reckoner for this purpose. 0.5 The table and inter-conversion charts included in this standard have been drawn up on the basis ol information and assistance derived from the inter-conversion charts for aqueous ethyl alcohol published in American Perfume and Cosmetics Journal 1965, 80, May, P 32. 0.6 In reporting the result of a test made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with the latest version of IS: 2-1960:.
*Tables for alcoholometry. tTables for aboholometry ( by Pyknometer method ). SRules for rounding off numerical values ( rev&d ). 3

X3:5860-1070

Ia1 This standard includes Table 1 and three inter-conversion charts ( Fig. 1 to 3 ) intended for use in the inter-conversion of various units used in the estimation of percentages of ethanol in ethanol-water mix~1nre.s.
1.1.X Table 1 shows the inter-relationship a) specific gravity in air at 15.6"/15-6�C b) c) d) e) f) percentage of British proof spirit, percentage of ethanol by weight, percentage of ethanol by volume at 15*6"j156"C, percentage of US proof spirit, arid specific gravity in vacuum at 1,5'/15"C. between:

1.1.2 The values in Table 1 and the three charts [ Fig. 1 to 3 (p. 69-71)] are calculated by rounding approximate>>: to the fourth decimal places in the case of specific gravities and to the second decimal places in the case of other units.
